propositions: The T11 post-rollback schema state paragraph generates near-identical tautological findings that are meaningless against an append-only store, drowning rare real catches.

The unconditional post-rollback paragraph is replaced with a four-condition applicability rule that raises findings only when a plan reinterprets, rewrites/migrates in place, removes/narrows a read path, or performs a one-way transformation.
An anti-false-positive line exempts purely additive backward-compatible persistence changes (new types, optional fields, defaulted columns) that existing readers ignore.
The applicability rule names no store technology so it applies to SQL migrations, event stores, document databases, and config formats.
The operator rejected a per-plan finding cap in favor of removing the tautology class at its source; the posture remains advisory.
Contract tests assert presence of the four conditions and the anti-FP line, absence of the old wording, and that the rule names no store technology; the criteria guide is regenerated.
